humanities_role_explanation: The benchmark is designed by professional historians specifically to evaluate disciplinary historical reasoning and research methodologies (such as paleography, epigraphy, source criticism, and cultural contextualization) rather than using historical material as raw data for generic linguistic tasks.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Combines a variety of modalities reflecting actual archival research, including printed text, digitized manuscript scans, historical maps, inscriptions, oral history audio recordings, and documentary video clips.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Tests tasks modeled on historical scholarship, including the transcription of cursive/damaged manuscripts (HTR/OCR repair), translation of dead or low-resource languages, temporal reasoning, iconographic interpretation of visual art, cultural contextualization of source materials, and dating/attribution of ancient epigraphic monuments.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Specifically scoped to evaluating historical reasoning and research capabilities in the discipline of history.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: Evaluates several state-of-the-art models including GPT-4o, DeepSeek-R1, o3, o4-mini-high, and Grok 3.

quantitative_metrics.note: Uses pass@1 and pass@2 accuracy, evaluated via an LLM judge and verified by human expert review.

published_after_march_2023.note: The preprint paper was published in June 2025.

summary: This paper introduces HistBench, a comprehensive benchmark containing 414 high-quality, expert-reviewed questions across 29 languages designed to evaluate AI's historical reasoning capabilities under real-world research constraints. The authors also present HistAgent, a domain-specialized AI agent equipped with modular tools for manuscript OCR, multi-step literature retrieval, translation, and reverse image search designed to mirror the workflow of human historians. Experimental evaluation shows that HistAgent substantially outperforms both generic LLMs with online search and generalist agents on HistBench, GAIA, and the Humanity's Last Exam history subset.
key_findings: HistAgent based on GPT-4o achieved 27.54% pass@1 and 36.47% pass@2 accuracy on HistBench, significantly outperforming GPT-4o with web search (18.60%) and open Deep Research agents (25.12% pass@2). HistAgent also demonstrated robust out-of-domain generalization, scoring 60.00% accuracy on the GAIA validation set and 28.57% on the HLE History subset.
facets_explanation: The benchmark's 414 questions were authored by over 40 history experts, including professors, PhD students, and research assistants from institutions like Fudan and Princeton. Answering these tasks requires extensive historical background knowledge external to the provided visual or textual stimulus. Although a multi-stage review pipeline was used to filter out ambiguous questions, the paper does not systematically address how inter-annotator disagreement or competing historical interpretations were treated.
